## Colombia in 9 days: Bogotá, Medellín and Cartagena with a coffee estate visit

This itinerary follows a clear progression: first, history and coffee around [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/); then urban culture and mountain scenery in [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/); and finally, colonial architecture and the Caribbean coast in [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/). The journey lasts **9 days and 8 nights**, with flights between the main cities.

What sets it apart from a standard city tour is a dedicated day at [Hacienda Coloma coffee estate](/colombia/place/hacienda-coloma/), a visit to [Lake Guatavita](/colombia/place/lake-guatavita/) and the underground Salt Cathedral in [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/). In one trip, you can experience how Colombia's landscapes and everyday life change from a high-altitude plateau to the Caribbean Sea.

The itinerary suits travelers who want to explore cultural landmarks and taste Colombian coffee where it is grown and processed. It does not include long mountain hikes or a multi-day beach holiday.

## First 4 days: Bogotá, coffee production and the surrounding area

On the first day, you are met on arrival and transferred to your hotel. It is a good opportunity to get acquainted with the city without a demanding sightseeing schedule.

**Day 2 is all about coffee.** From Bogotá, travelers head toward Fusagasugá to visit Hacienda Coloma. Here, you learn about growing coffee, harvesting, processing and roasting the beans, followed by a tasting. The day also includes a tasting of aged rum and a lunch of local dishes. This is a substantial, standalone part of the journey: coffee takes up an entire day rather than appearing only on the hotel breakfast menu.

On **day 3**, sightseeing takes place in historic Bogotá. The tour covers La Candelaria, the Gold Museum, the Botero Museum and Monserrate. Together, these places reveal different periods: pre-Columbian metalworking, colonial architecture and modern art. Pay attention to museum opening schedules: the itinerary contains specific notes about closure days, so the order of visits matters when choosing your travel dates.

On **day 4**, travelers visit [Guatavita](/colombia/place/lake-guatavita/) and Zipaquirá. The lake is associated with the legend of El Dorado, while the Salt Cathedral is an entirely different attraction: an underground space created inside a salt mine. This is a long sightseeing day with road transfers, so leaving the evening free after returning is sensible.

## Days 5–6: Medellín and Guatapé

On day 5, you fly from Bogotá to Medellín and travel to [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/). Here stands the El Peñón rock, rising above a network of reservoirs. The excursion combines sweeping natural views with a walk through a town known for its brightly decorated facades.

Climbing the steps to the top of the rock requires physical fitness and depends on the itinerary selected. Travelers who need to limit physical exertion should discuss the length of the walk before departure to keep their visit to Guatapé comfortable.

**Day 6 is dedicated to Medellín itself.** Sightseeing includes Fernando Botero's sculpture square, the Museum of Antioquia, Comuna 13 and the castle museum. The city is compelling for the way its contemporary cultural life exists alongside a difficult history. It is better to devote a full day to this part of the itinerary than try to combine it with the longer excursion to Guatapé.

## Final 3 days: colonial Cartagena

On day 7, travelers fly to Cartagena. The main sightseeing tour takes place **on day 8**. It covers historic streets, the old city's fortifications, the Bocagrande district, La Popa hill and San Felipe de Barajas Fortress.

The fortification system of [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) is part of the UNESCO World Heritage property “Port, Fortresses and Group of Monuments, Cartagena.” A walk through the city is therefore an encounter with the history of one of the colonial era's most important ports, rather than simply an afternoon among colorful facades.

Day 9 includes breakfast and a transfer to the airport. A full, separate beach day on the Rosario Islands **is not part of this itinerary**. If you would like time by the sea, compare this trip with options that include the [Rosario Islands](/colombia/place/rosario-islands/) as a standalone excursion.

## Transport, meals and price: what is confirmed

The tour price is **$3729**, and the duration is 9 days / 8 nights. The itinerary is designed as a private journey. The list of inclusions specifically names the domestic flights **Bogotá — Medellín — Cartagena** and meals according to the itinerary; arrival assistance, transfers and sightseeing days are also described.

To compare this offer with other tours, check the exact hotel category, room and accommodation arrangement, guide language, admission tickets for individual attractions and meals included on each day. **Do not automatically assume services from other Colombian itineraries are included**, even when they visit the same three cities.

| Stage | Defining experiences |
|---|---|
| Bogotá, 4 days | Museums, coffee, Guatavita and Zipaquirá |
| Medellín, 2 days | Guatapé and urban culture |
| Cartagena, 3 days | Colonial city and departure |

The journey involves frequent travel but no multi-day trekking. Airports and flights will take up part of the schedule. For a more leisurely introduction to coffee or time at the beach, explore other options on the [Colombia tours page](/colombia/tour/) and in the [collection of coffee journeys](/interests/coffee-tours/tours/colombia/).

## How the nine-day itinerary differs from other trips

The [six-day “Bogotá and Cartagena” trip](/colombia/tour/colombia-bogota-cartagena-culture-6-days-2024/) focuses on two cities and the Rosario Islands but does not include Medellín or a dedicated coffee day at Coloma. The [fifteen-day journey featuring the Lost City](/colombia/tour/colombia-bogota-cartagena-medellin-rosario-islands-santa-marta/) is much longer and includes a multi-day trek through the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta.

**Nine days is a good choice for a cultural journey through three cities with an in-depth introduction to coffee.** A different trip is needed for active trekking, while a dedicated beach holiday is better served by adding nights on the Caribbean coast.

## Frequently asked questions about the 9-day Colombia tour

### Is a coffee farm visit included?

Yes. The itinerary dedicates a full day to [Hacienda Coloma](/colombia/place/hacienda-coloma/), with an introduction to coffee production and a tasting.

### Does the itinerary include Medellín and Guatapé?

Yes. After flying to Medellín, you visit El Peñón rock and Guatapé, followed by a city tour of Medellín the next day.

### Are domestic flights included?

The price includes flights from Bogotá to Medellín and onward to Cartagena. Other flights and your international arrival arrangements must be considered separately according to the itinerary.

### Are the Rosario Islands included?

There is no standalone trip to the Rosario Islands during these 9 days. For a marine excursion, compare [other Colombia tours](/colombia/tour/).

### How much time is spent in Cartagena?

The itinerary includes arrival, a separate sightseeing day and departure on day 9. For several full days on the Caribbean coast, choose a longer trip.

## Coffee, Bogotá, Medellín and Cartagena in 10 days: who is this tour for?

**The defining feature of this journey is a full day at Hacienda Coloma coffee estate within an itinerary linking three of Colombia's major cities.** Over 10 days and 9 nights, you will explore the capital, visit the area around Lake Guatavita, see Medellín's street art and finish on the Caribbean coast.

It is a good introduction to the country for travelers who want to understand its history and taste coffee where it is grown, without devoting their entire holiday to plantations. The coffee experience takes **one day**, while the remaining stops focus on museums, architecture, nature and city life.

Unlike the [12-day tour with San Andrés Island](/colombia/tour/colombia-highlights-beaches-12-days/), this trip has no three-day island break. The [14-day itinerary including the Coffee Region and Tayrona](/colombia/tour/iconic-colombia-14-days/) covers more of the country and follows a different travel route.

## What makes the coffee visit to Hacienda Coloma special?

The excursion departs from [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), while [Hacienda Coloma](/colombia/place/hacienda-coloma/) is located near [Fusagasugá](/colombia/place/fusagasuga/). The journey from the capital takes approximately 120 minutes according to the itinerary. It is an opportunity to visit a coffee-growing estate without another flight or an overnight stay in the western Andes.

During the visit, you explore the stages of coffee cultivation and production: from seeds and coffee trees to harvesting, processing the beans and brewing the drink. After the main tour, there is a tasting of aged rum with coffee notes and a local lunch. Travelers then return to Bogotá.

**Do not confuse this day with a full journey through Colombia's Coffee Triangle.** The areas around [Pereira](/colombia/place/pereira/), [Salento](/colombia/place/salento/) and the [Cocora Valley](/colombia/place/cocora-valley/) lie in another part of the country. Trips there generally combine farms, mountain scenery and small towns. On this ten-day itinerary, the main coffee experience takes place at Coloma; the western Coffee Region is not included.

For other ways to explore Colombia's coffee heritage, see the [coffee tours section](/interests/coffee-tours/).

## How is time divided between the cities?

| Part of the trip | Experiences |
|---|---|
| Days 1–4 | Bogotá, Coloma, Guatavita, Zipaquirá |
| Days 5–6 | Medellín, Guatapé |
| Days 7–10 | Cartagena, a free day and departure |

In the capital, sightseeing includes the Gold Museum, the Botero Museum, historic neighborhoods and a trip up Monserrate. An excursion outside the city combines [Lake Guatavita](/colombia/place/lake-guatavita/), known for the El Dorado legend, with the [Salt Cathedral in Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/).

Next comes a domestic flight to [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/). Sightseeing includes the Museum of Antioquia, Botero's sculptures, Comuna 13 and [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) with El Peñón rock. These are two days of excursions, so longer independent trips around Medellín would need to be arranged separately.

The last stop is [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/). The scheduled sightseeing includes the historic center, San Felipe de Barajas Fortress and a viewpoint on La Popa hill. Day 9 is free: you can spend it strolling at your own pace or by the sea. However, the trip **does not offer several full beach days** as the San Andrés itinerary does.

## Travel arrangements and conditions to consider

The price includes **domestic flights from Bogotá to Medellín and Medellín to Cartagena**, excursions with a Russian-speaking guide, and meals as specified in the itinerary. International airfare, additional excursions, excess baggage and extra drinks are charged separately. Check the exact meal arrangements and other conditions in the tour description rather than assuming full board.

The first few days take place at altitude. Bogotá sits high in the Andes, while the area around Guatavita reaches roughly 3,100 meters above sea level. After a long flight, it helps to rest, stay hydrated and assess how you feel before a long walk. The climate and clothing requirements then change: Medellín is warmer, while Cartagena has Caribbean heat and humidity.

**Who will particularly enjoy this trip?** Travelers interested in urban culture, coffee production and the contrast between the Andes and the Caribbean coast. Those wanting several nights on a coffee farm, strenuous wilderness trekking or an extended beach holiday should compare other [Colombia tours](/colombia/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about the ten-day coffee tour

### Is this a specialist tour exclusively for coffee lovers?

No. One day is devoted to a coffee estate. The main itinerary covers three cities, museums, historic quarters and natural and architectural landmarks.

### Does the trip visit the actual Coffee Region near Pereira?

No. The Hacienda Coloma visit departs from Bogotá and takes place near Fusagasugá. Pereira and the Cocora Valley are not included in this ten-day itinerary.

### Do I need to buy domestic flights myself?

Flights from Bogotá to Medellín and from Medellín to Cartagena are listed among the included services. International airfare is paid separately.

### Can the final days be considered a full beach holiday?

There is one free day in Cartagena without a scheduled excursion. For several days on an island, consider the [San Andrés itinerary](/colombia/tour/colombia-highlights-beaches-12-days/).

## Colombia in 8 days: Bogotá, Medellín and Cartagena with the Rosario Islands

The itinerary combines **3 nights in [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), 2 in [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/) and 2 in [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/)**. Departure is scheduled for day eight. This journey introduces three sides of Colombia: its high-altitude capital, the urban heritage of Antioquia and a fortified Caribbean port. Excursions outside the cities lead to Zipaquirá's underground cathedral, the granite rock near Guatapé and the Rosario Islands.

Each stop offers a distinctly different experience. In Bogotá, the focus is on history and museum collections. In Medellín, it is the urban environment, sculpture and the transformation of neighborhoods. Cartagena brings the journey to a close with colonial fortifications and a day on the water.

## First stage: three nights in Bogotá

After arrival and transfer, the following day features a tour of historic La Candelaria. The itinerary includes the Gold Museum, Casa de la Moneda, art collections associated with Fernando Botero, Bolívar Square and a trip up Monserrate. It is a full day: the tour lasts approximately **6 hours**.

Museum opening hours matter when choosing dates. **The Gold Museum is closed on Mondays**, as confirmed by the official Banco de la República schedule. Some other collection museums are also closed on Tuesdays. If a sightseeing day coincides with a closure, the order of visits should be agreed in advance; entry to every gallery cannot be promised on every day of the week without checking.

Day three includes an excursion to [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/) and its Salt Cathedral inside a mine. According to the published itinerary, the excursion lasts about **5 hours** and includes private transportation, an English-speaking guide and admission. The underground setting is a sharp contrast to the capital's museums: here the cultural attraction was created inside former mining galleries.

## Medellín: Comuna 13, sculptures and Guatapé

Day four begins with a flight from Bogotá to [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/). After arrival, a seven-hour city sightseeing tour is planned, including stops across the city and a visit to Comuna 13. The neighborhood's contemporary murals offer a way to understand the city's history through works created by local residents; the walk also takes in the famous outdoor escalators.

The next day, the route leaves the city for [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) and the Piedra del Peñol rock. The drive follows local roads, taking in Guatapé's decorated facades and the reservoir. The excursion lasts approximately **8 hours** and includes a traditional lunch and a ride around town by motorcycle taxi.

An important distinction separates the included itinerary from optional activities: **climbing the rock itself and taking a boat trip on the reservoir cost extra**, although sightseeing in Guatapé is already part of the day. The Peñol and Guatapé excursion is listed in Spanish, while most other city sightseeing days are led by English-speaking guides. Do not assume all eight days will be guided in Russian without separate arrangements.

## Cartagena and a day on the Rosario Islands

Day six features a flight to [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) and a city tour covering San Felipe de Barajas Fortress, the Clock Tower and the old center. Cartagena's historic fortifications form part of a UNESCO World Heritage site. Rather than a brief look at its squares, the day offers a chance to understand the city as a former major Caribbean port.

Day seven is reserved for the [Rosario Islands](/colombia/place/rosario-islands/). According to the itinerary, the group departs from the Bodeguita pier by speedboat; a typical Caribbean lunch and free time by the sea are included. It is a **group excursion**, even if the main city tours are private.

Important exclusions: the **Coralia port tax of $10** and **oceanarium admission of $10** are paid separately. Diving and snorkeling are listed as optional activities at additional cost, not mandatory parts of the day. Sea conditions can affect the crossing.

## Budget and transportation

| Leg | What to allow for |
|---|---|
| Bogotá — Medellín | Domestic flight paid separately |
| Medellín — Cartagena | Domestic flight paid separately |
| Rosario Islands | Group boat trip; additional fees |

The starting tour price is **$1725**, but this is not the full trip cost once flights are added. International and domestic flights are listed under “Not included.” Accommodation for 7 nights, breakfasts and the specified excursions are included in the package. Tips, personal expenses and meals not listed are paid separately.

Day eight is dedicated to the transfer to Cartagena airport. When purchasing international flights, it is sensible to coordinate domestic flight times and baggage collection arrangements. Ada Tours helps align the sequence of excursions and transfers with the flights selected.

## Who is this tour for, and when should you choose another?

This eight-day option suits travelers who want to see Bogotá, Medellín and Cartagena while leaving one day for the Caribbean Sea. There are many excursions and few completely free days. Be prepared for early transfers and packed sightseeing schedules.

If coffee production and rural scenery are your priorities, compare the [nine-day itinerary through the Coffee Region](/colombia/tour/colombia-bogota-eje-cafetero-cartagena-9-days/). If you are more interested in Bogotá, Guatavita and the cities without an island day, there is [another nine-day Colombia itinerary](/colombia/tour/colombia-bogota-cartagena-medellin-zipaquira-guatape/). Browse the full selection in the [Colombia tours catalog](/colombia/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about the 8-day tour

### Are domestic flights included?

No. Flights from Bogotá to Medellín and Medellín to Cartagena are paid separately.

### Will there be a Russian-speaking guide every day?

Most excursions are conducted by English-speaking guides, while the trip to Guatapé is guided in Spanish. A different language arrangement must be agreed separately.

### Is the climb up Piedra del Peñol included?

No. It is excluded from the Guatapé excursion price.

### Are the Rosario Islands included in the itinerary?

Yes. A group boat excursion with lunch is scheduled; port fees and certain activities cost extra.

After Bogotá and the Chicaque cloud forest, travelers fly to La Macarena, spend 3 nights at La Manigua nature lodge and explore trails in the river's upper and lower basins. ## Caño Cristales: why allow 8 days?

The main destination on this itinerary is [Caño Cristales](/colombia/place/cano-cristales/), known for its stretches of colorful riverbed. Bright red, green and other hues are linked to aquatic vegetation, lighting conditions and water levels. Here, **the season and the permitted visiting route** matter more than chasing a particular photographic viewpoint.

The opening days introduce [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) and the cloud forest of [Chicaque Park](/colombia/place/chicaque-park/). Travelers then fly to [La Macarena](/colombia/place/la-macarena/) and spend 3 nights at La Manigua nature lodge. Separate days are dedicated to the upper and lower sections of the river; the following day brings wildlife watching along the [Guayabero](/colombia/place/guayabero-river/) before the flight back to the capital.

Unlike [sightseeing tours of Colombia's cities](/colombia/tour/), this itinerary involves hiking on trails and rocky ground. It is for travelers who enjoy nature and active walks rather than a sequence of museums and beach stops.

## The 2027 season and access to the colorful river

The proposed travel season runs **from June 1 to November 30, 2027**. Charter departures to La Macarena are scheduled from Monday through Thursday; specific dates and flight times depend on flight operations and permits. These are the dates of the 2027 offer and do not guarantee identical natural conditions every day.

The colors of Caño Cristales depend on the condition of its aquatic vegetation, water clarity and the rainy season. The most intense colors cannot be guaranteed for any particular day in advance. Colombia's national parks regulate access to river sections for conservation purposes, so the permitted route may change.

**When choosing dates, check 2 separate things:** flight availability and permission to visit particular parts of the protected natural area. Even a confirmed arrival in La Macarena does not replace the park briefing and its rules. If your goal is to photograph a specific cascade, do not assume its visit is unconditionally included.

## Getting to the river: canoe, four-wheel drive and hiking trail

After the **Bogotá — La Macarena** charter flight, the first outing includes a canoe trip along the [Guayabero](/colombia/place/guayabero-river/), a stop at the El Mirador viewpoint and a visit to [Caño Cristalitos](/colombia/place/cano-cristalitos/). This is a gradual introduction to the local natural environment and visiting rules before the main excursions to Caño Cristales.

The next 2 days focus on different sections of the colorful river. A typical route combines a boat, a stretch by 4×4 vehicle and an approach on foot. **Trekking in the upper basin takes about 5–7 hours, with trails described as 8–13 km long.** It is a genuine physical challenge in a hot, humid climate, even though the route does not involve technical mountaineering.

On the lower section, travelers also walk among rocks, natural pools and vegetation. The itinerary includes authorized swimming spots, but park staff determine whether swimming is actually permitted. The Los Ochos formations can be seen from the opposite bank; a separate visit to Los Ochos is not confirmed.

This type of trip may not suit people with limited mobility or difficulty walking long distances. Before purchasing, assess the daily distances and your ability to cross uneven trails without the support of urban infrastructure.

## Three nights at La Manigua: accommodation and facilities

The complete itinerary lasts **8 days and 7 nights**: 4 nights in Bogotá and 3 at La Manigua lodge near La Macarena. The lodge is located close to the natural area that is the main focus of the journey. It offers simple, clean and comfortable accommodation; a **luxury standard has not been confirmed**.

Travelers stay in the La Macarena area for several consecutive days, returning from the river routes to their lodge. This portion of the itinerary includes 3 breakfasts, 3 lunches and 3 dinners. In Bogotá, 4 breakfasts are included; other meals depend on the specific day and conditions.

Before traveling to La Macarena, arrange to carry Colombian pesos in cash. The stated conditions specifically mention limited currency-exchange options, and cash availability at local ATMs may be unreliable. It is better to take care of this before flying out of the capital.

Also check baggage limits for the charter flight, facilities for charging electronic devices and actual mobile coverage. These should not be assumed to match the conditions at your Bogotá hotel unless confirmed for the chosen departure.

## Chicaque and Guayabero: natural experiences beyond the main river

The second natural highlight is [Chicaque Park](/colombia/place/chicaque-park/) near Bogotá. The visit includes a walk through cloud forest with a specialist local guide. Trails are uneven, and the walk takes several hours. **The guide in Chicaque speaks Spanish**, while the main itinerary provides English-speaking assistance.

Toward the end of the La Macarena stay, a morning canoe outing is planned on the [Guayabero](/colombia/place/guayabero-river/). Birds and other animals can be seen along the banks; under favorable conditions, river dolphins may also appear. Wildlife does not follow a timetable, so such an encounter cannot be promised as a guaranteed service.

One evening includes meeting local residents and learning to make chocolate from cocoa beans. This adds another meaningful experience, but it does not replace the journey's central purpose: visiting the protected natural area of Caño Cristales.

## What is included in the price, and how to choose a rate

Unlike many city tours, this itinerary **includes the Bogotá — La Macarena — Bogotá charter flights**. It also includes private transfers, hotels and the lodge, local excursions, conservation fees, admission tickets, some meals and a local medical insurance card. International flights and expenses outside the specified inclusions are not covered.

Rates are quoted per person and differ by categories C, S and P and accommodation type SGL/DBL/TRP. The lowest price, **$4078**, applies to category **C with TRP**. In that same category, DBL costs $4586 and SGL costs $6539. Triple occupancy does not necessarily mean 3 separate beds. A price quoted without the category and number of guests can be misleading.

| Question | Itinerary details |
|---|---|
| Duration | 8 days / 7 nights |
| Lodge near La Macarena | 3 nights |
| Charter flights | Included |
| Maximum stated trail length | 13 km |
| Main guiding language | English |
| Season offered | June–November 2027 |

Special rules apply inside the protected area: the tour description specifies restrictions on alcohol, cigarettes, insect repellent and sunscreen while visiting the trails. Agree suitable clothing and permitted protection measures with the organizer ahead of time to keep your skin protected and yourself comfortable. Do not drink water from natural sources.

## Who will enjoy the Caño Cristales expedition?

**Choose this journey for active nature experiences** if you are comfortable walking on uneven trails and are prepared for changes to the plan due to weather or decisions by conservation authorities. It offers separate outings to different sections of the river and several nights close to the protected area, making it very different from a short city sightseeing trip.

Travelers more interested in history, colonial architecture and the sea may prefer [five days in Bogotá and Cartagena](/colombia/tour/colombia-essential-5-days/) or the [seven-day itinerary with Medellín](/colombia/tour/colombia-highlights-7-days/). To compare nature-focused programs, see [Colombia wildlife journeys](/interests/wildlife/tours/colombia/) and [adventure itineraries](/interests/adventure/tours/colombia/).

## Frequently asked questions about visiting Caño Cristales

### When is this tour scheduled?

The season runs from June 1 to November 30, **2027**. Exact dates depend on charter flights and permission to enter the protected natural area.

### How demanding are the hikes?

Upper-basin trails are described as **8–13 km** long and take approximately **5–7 hours**. There are also walks to other natural attractions and an excursion in Chicaque Park.

### Is the flight to La Macarena included?

Yes. The inclusions specify the Bogotá — La Macarena — Bogotá flight. International airfare is paid separately.

### Can I count on seeing river dolphins?

There is no guarantee. Animals, including dolphins, may be spotted on the Guayabero, but their appearance depends on natural conditions.

### Is the tour suitable for travelers who want to avoid physical exertion?

No. Visiting the main sections of Caño Cristales requires extended walking on natural trails. Discuss mobility limitations and any health considerations before booking.

## Caño Cristales and Colombia in 12 days: who will enjoy this trip?

This journey combines 4 distinct landscapes and ways of experiencing the country: high-altitude [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), the [La Macarena](/colombia/place/la-macarena/) area, coffee-growing slopes near [Pereira](/colombia/place/pereira/) and Caribbean [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/). The main reason to choose the itinerary is several days around [Caño Cristales](/colombia/place/cano-cristales/), where travelers reach natural sites by boat, four-wheel-drive vehicles and on foot.

The tour lasts 12 days and 11 nights. It suits travelers prepared for early departures, domestic flights and walks over rocky trails. A different option for a shorter introduction focused mainly on cities is [8 days in Bogotá, Medellín and Cartagena](/colombia/tour/colombia-capitals/), without a nature expedition to La Macarena.

## When to visit the colorful river and what depends on permits

The brilliant colors of Caño Cristales are produced by the aquatic plant Macarenia clavigera. They are especially visible in the rainy season when water levels and lighting are suitable. It makes sense to choose travel dates primarily around the natural part of the itinerary: the month alone cannot guarantee that the colorful riverbed will be visible.

The first nature-focused day starts with a charter flight from Bogotá to La Macarena. However, the first excursion does not necessarily lead to the main channel of Caño Cristales: environmental authorities may assign Caño Cristalitos, Caño Piedra or Río Bajo Lozada instead. The next day includes a full excursion to the colorful river, with another morning nature outing before the return flight.

Reaching the river involves a boat trip along the Guayabero, off-road transportation and hiking. **The exact trail, its availability and its duration are determined by local conservation authorities.** It would therefore be inaccurate to promise access to a particular section or a visit to a specific natural pool in advance.

Bring comfortable shoes with good grip, protection against sun and rain, and a willingness to cope with humid weather. Rules for entering protected areas must be checked before travel; they may differ from the conditions of an ordinary national park walk.

## Why visit other regions before and after La Macarena?

Sightseeing in [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) covers the historic La Candelaria district, the Gold Museum, the Botero collection and Bolívar Square. A separate day takes you to [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/) and its Salt Cathedral, and to [Lake Guatavita](/colombia/place/lake-guatavita/), associated with the El Dorado legend.

In the Coffee Region, excursions combine [Salento](/colombia/place/salento/), the [Cocora Valley](/colombia/place/cocora-valley/) and its wax palms, and a farm near [Santa Rosa de Cabal](/colombia/place/santa-rosa-de-cabal/). You learn about coffee growing and processing and then relax at a thermal spa complex. This offers a different kind of nature experience from the trails at Caño Cristales.

The journey ends in [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/), where the historic center, San Felipe de Barajas Fortress and a separate trip to the [Rosario Islands](/colombia/place/rosario-islands/) are scheduled. The day at sea comes at the end of a busy itinerary and is not the same as a multi-day beach holiday.

## Flights and inclusions: what to check in the quotation

The tour includes **Bogotá — La Macarena — Bogotá charter air tickets**. Flights from Bogotá to Pereira, from Pereira to Cartagena, and international flights are paid separately. Airport-to-hotel and hotel-to-airport transfers are planned in each city.

The nights are divided as follows: 4 in Bogotá, 2 in La Macarena, 3 in Pereira and 2 in Cartagena. Included meals comprise 11 breakfasts, 5 lunches during excursions and 2 dinners in La Macarena. For travelers staying in a single room, some excursions may operate in a group format, even though other outings are planned privately.

Personal expenses, tips, additional meals and extra activities are paid separately. Additional fees and possible oceanarium admission charges are listed for the Rosario Islands outing. When agreeing on travel dates, it is important to check both the availability of nature excursions and connections between domestic flights.

## Frequently asked questions about the Caño Cristales journey

### Can I choose the trail and waterfalls in advance?

No. Specific nature routes are set by environmental authorities according to current permits. The itinerary specifies the days, transport and general nature excursions, but the exact areas visited can change.

### Is it possible to avoid hiking?

The main excursion involves walking after the boat and four-wheel-drive sections. If you have limited mobility, discuss the permitted route and physical requirements before booking.

### Are all domestic flights included?

No. The Bogotá — La Macarena — Bogotá charter is included. Tickets to Pereira and Cartagena are calculated separately.

### Is there time by the sea at the end?

Yes. The itinerary has a full day on the Rosario Islands. If you would prefer several nights directly by the sea, consider the [Barú Island tour](/colombia/tour/colombia-vip-coffee-cartagena-baru-10-days/).
